tail:
Authored and registered all seven assigned items in dependency order: the scaling definition, integer-pairing lemma, A2, B2/C2 and G2 examples, the finite-type theorem, and the I2(5) counterexample. The three examples compute at level 10. The A/B pages, plan entries, manifests, coverage records and contracts are updated. No new prerequisite items were needed.

The G2 proof computes the twelve-root orbit and verifies the root-system axioms locally. I corrected its scaffold’s sample pairing: \(B(a_t,(3a_s+2a_t)^\vee)=+1\); a correct \(-1\) example uses \(3a_s+a_t\). I checked the classification and root-configuration references in [Milne](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/LAG.pdf), [Knapp](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~aknapp/download/Beyond2-clickable.pdf), and [Michel](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~jean.michel/papiers/cox.pdf).

All seven items pass precheck and strict proof contracts; rendering passed for seven items and both pages, content policy passed for seven items, and focused depcheck passed on the 908-item closure. Manifest dependencies and pair-scoped plan validation pass. The required final proof-layout check passed: **7 items, 70 steps, 0 defects**.

Two item decisions remain escalated: the finite-type theorem and I2(5) counterexample use a batch-13 classification proof whose step 1.4 identity is false at \(i=2\) (2, not 3). Their exact consuming steps and the correction are in the [authoring report](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/frontier-42-coxeter-32-step3b-pair-crystallographic-root-lattices-and-weyl-group-interfaces.md). The run-wide dependency-level check also found nine stale levels in other items, and run-wide plan validation found missing item assignments and undeclared prerequisites in other pairs; the report lists them. The owned items’ levels match. I left the unified cross-batch ledger refresh to the serial reconciler.
